named_subject: a horse's head and neck, with a jagged mane, two pointed ears, an eye and a jaw line
action: The horse's head starts upright, swings its muzzle forward and down toward the right through the middle frames, comes back up, and in the last four frames is redrawn smaller and lower in the frame with grass zigzags along the bottom.
identity_gap: The animated head uses the doodle's parts (zigzag mane, two leaf-shaped ears, scribbled eye, cheek curve with jaw and throat lines) in the same single-stroke style, but it is mirrored to face right and drawn with a long vertical face instead of the doodle's short wedge-shaped muzzle.
notes: Frames 1 to 11 follow the film's head turn and forward reach reasonably, but the film ends with the horse lowering its muzzle into the hay, while the animation's frames 13 to 16 keep the head upright and only shrink it, with a size and position jump between frames 12 and 13. The change that would help most is to keep the head at a constant scale and rotate the muzzle down to the hay at the bottom of the frame in frames 12 to 16, as the film does.
